feature: Customer Portal v2 -- the OWNERSHIP matrix (/portal-v2/ownership), recreated from 'Ownership.dc.html', a file that did not exist in the round-one handoff at all. Four names (Responsible / Accountable / Consulted / Informed) against twenty-four objects across seven types, five derived counters above the matrix, and four detail panels behind them. PART 10 finished the deferred slide-overs: the assign slide-over's own surface (Mark accepted / Who held it before / Leave unassigned -- record it as a gap), the add-a-row flow, delegation + handover, the row detail, and 'What ownership drives' (routing). Every number on screen is derived from one fixture (ownershipData.ts) by ownershipModel.ts and pinned by 78 unit assertions; this manifest proves the DOM actually shows what those derivations return.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the five login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the page.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/ownership. App.tsx declares '/portal-v2/ownership/:type' and '/portal-v2/ownership' BEFORE '/portal-v2/:pillar' so the param route cannot swallow them.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree. This manifest cannot pass until the commit it was written against is deployed.

ROUND TWO, ITEM 4 IS WHAT OWN9-OWN14 EXIST FOR. The changelog: the five counters 'changed from pill-shaped inline buttons to box-shaped cards in a fixed 5-column grid (repeat(5, 1fr)) so they never wrap to a second row; labels wrap to two lines instead of truncating'. Both halves are asserted -- all five labels are read out of ONE container, which is only possible if all five rendered, and the two longest labels are asserted in full rather than truncated. The grid itself is repeat(5,minmax(0,1fr)) rather than plain 1fr: they differ on a long label, and only the minmax form actually holds five columns instead of letting a wide word push a track out.

ROUND TWO, ITEM 2: Ownership no longer has its own People & roles button or slide-over. The prototype confirms the removal twice -- there is no people-editing markup left in the file, and `peopleRows` is still COMPUTED at Ownership.dc.html 1032 with nothing rendering it. OWN30 asserts that no such control exists here. Stated plainly: an `absent` assertion on a testid this build never rendered passes trivially, so OWN30 is a REINTRODUCTION GUARD rather than evidence of a removal. The assertion that actually carries weight is OWN31-OWN35, which proves the editing works from its NEW home and reaches this page.

THERE IS NO NEGATIVE TEXT ASSERTION IN THIS HARNESS, and an array in `textContains` is ANY-of, not all-of (UiTestExecutor.cs:570, :1282). Every all-of assertion here is its own step, and absence is asserted on a selector rather than on text.

THE PROP CONTRACT IS PROVED ACROSS TWO PAGES. OWN31-OWN35 rename a person in Settings and then read the NEW name out of the Ownership matrix. That is the README's 'the Ownership matrix reads the same data live' sentence, and it is the one assertion that would fail if the people list were duplicated per page instead of shared.

OWN34 MUST BE A CLICK, NOT A `goto`, AND THE FIRST RUN PROVED IT. Written with `goto` this sequence failed 41/42: the matrix still read 'Priya Raman'. `goto` drives the WebView2 to a URL, which is a FULL PAGE LOAD, and the people list is client-only state with no endpoint behind it yet, so a reload resets it to the seed. That is correct behaviour, not a bug -- the prototype persists nothing either -- but it means a `goto` between the edit and the assertion tests the seed rather than the sharing. The sidebar nav row is a client-side wouter Link, so clicking it preserves the store and is also how a customer actually gets there. WHEN A REAL PEOPLE ENDPOINT LANDS, this step can go back to `goto` and should then still pass; if it does not, the persistence is not wired.

WHY THE COUNTS ARE THE NUMBERS THEY ARE: 6 gaps (svc-copilot, CR-0149, RSK-004, ANN-teams-recap, ANN-share, ANN-copilot), 3 duty conflicts (CE-AUTH has Shane McCaw as both R and A; INC-2274 has the Service desk GROUP as Responsible; Dan Whitlock is Accountable for 14 of 24, a strict majority), 0 carrying too much (Marcus is away but HAS a deputy, so nothing warns -- the zero is the correct answer, not a missing feature), 4 not in the matrix, 24 objects.

NO `select` STEPS ANYWHERE. UiTestExecutor.cs takes the `value` setter from HTMLInputElement.prototype for anything that is not a TEXTAREA, so invoking it on a native <select> throws 'Illegal invocation'; and an unrecognised action falls through and SILENTLY PASSES. This page has no <select> in its main flow -- the assign form's dropdown lives in the right drawer and is deliberately not driven here.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.
